INSTRUCTIONS PERTAINING TO RISK OF FIRE, ELECTRIC SHOCK, OR INJURY TO PERSONS

• Read all the instructions before using the product. • Do not allow children to play with the product. Close supervision of children is necessary when the product is used near children. • Risk of electric shock may occur if using accessories that are not recommended or sold by professional product manufacturers. • When the product is not in use, unplug the power plug from the product's socket. • Do not dismantle the product, as this may lead to unpredictable risks such as fire, explosion, or electric shock. • Do not use the product with damaged cords, plugs, or output cables, as this may cause electric shock. • To ensure proper air circulation, keep the product vents uncovered. The area where the product is used must have adequate airflow in a cool, dry environment to prevent overheating. ◦Charging in damp or poorly ventilated spaces may cause safety hazards. ◦Water can cause short circuits or damage to the charger, leading to safety risks. • Do not expose the product to fire, high temperatures, direct sunlight, or high-heat environments such as inside a parked vehicle. Such exposure may result in fire or explosion. Always follow these basic precautions when using this product.

During the lifecycle of energy storage products, a certain degree of capacity and energy degradation is expected. As the number of charge and discharge cycles increases and storage time extends, this degradation will gradually intensify, which is a normal phenomenon consistent with the natural aging of battery cells.

Batteries and accumulators must not be disposed of with household waste. As a consumer, you are legally required to dispose of all batteries and accumulators at designated collection points, regardless of whether they contain hazardous substances. Please return used batteries and accumulators to a local collection point, recycling center, or to the retailer where they were purchased. Proper disposal ensures environmentally responsible recycling and prevents potential harm to human health and the environment.

To prevent unnecessary battery consumption caused by forgetting to turn off the output, Energy Saving Mode is enabled by default. If no device is connected or the connected device's power consumption is below a certain threshold (AC output ≤ 25W, USB + DC 12V port ≤ 2W ) for 6 hours, the product will automatically turn off the outputs. To turn Energy Saving Mode on or off, press and hold both the AC power button and the main power button for 3 seconds.

Green energy first: We advocate to use the green energy first. This product supports two modes of charging at the same time: solar charging and AC wall charging. When AC wall charging and solar charging are turned on at the same time, the product will give priority to solar charging and both methods will be used to charge the battery at the maximum permissible power.
Fully charge the product before its first use.

• The recommended charging temperature for the product ranges from 32°F to 113°F (0°C to 45°C), and the discharging temperature ranges from 5°F to 113°F (-15°C to 45°C). Operating the product beyond this temperature range may restrict its charging and discharging capabilities, or even prevent it from charging or discharging. • The charging power and battery capacity of the product may vary due to temperature fluctuations.

When the product is charged via the 65W AC Adapter or the USB-C port, the charging icon will not appear on the LCD screen. Please refer to the battery power indicator and input power displayed on the LCD to check the charging status.
Connect the included 65W AC adapter to the product’s DC8020 port and plug the adapter into a wall outlet.

Jackery Explorer 300 has one DC8020 input port and is compatible with the Jackery solar panels.

It is recommended to use the Jackery Solar Panel to charge the Explorer 300. Ensure that the open-circuit voltage (Voc) of the solar panel falls within the Jackery Explorer 300's DC input voltage range (16V–28V).
• Only one solar panel can be connected to the DC8020 input port. • Jackery is not responsible for any damage or loss resulting from the use of third-party solar panels.
This product can be charged using a 12V car charger. Ensure that the car charger and the 12V car power outlet provide a good connection.

• Please start the vehicle before charging your power station. • If the vehicle is running on bumpy roads, it is forbidden to use the car charger in case it causes non-standard operation. The Company will not be responsible for any loss caused by non-standard operation. • Vehicle charging is only applicable to vehicles with 12V DC, not 24V DC. Please do not charge this product in 24V vehicle to avoid personal injury and property loss.

Store the product in a dry clean place with proper ventilation. Storage temperature and humidity: • 1 month: -4°F to 113°F / -20°C to 45°C (0-60%RH) • 3 months: 32°F to 113°F / 0°C to 45°C (0-60%RH) • 12 months: 32°F to 77°F / 0°C to 25°C (0-60%RH) If this product is stored for a long period of time (3 months - 6 months) with the power depleted, it may become unchargeable. To prevent this and maintain battery health, it is recommended to check and recharge the product every three months and perform a full charge and discharge cycle at least once every 6 to 12 months.
If any of the following fault codes appear, follow the listed corrective actions to resolve the issue. If fault persists, please contact Jackery Customer Support.
Connect the product to loads to discharge its battery until the fault disappears.
Charge the product via solar panels or AC wall outlet until the fault disappears.

1. Wait for the grid to normalize before charging the product via AC wall outlet. 2. Check whether the air intake and exhaust vents are blocked; ensure 20 cm clearance on both side of the product. 3. Place the product in a shaded, well-ventilated area where the ambient temperature is below 45°C. 4.Disconnect all loads from the product, keep it idle and wait until the fault disappears. 5. Restart the product.

1. Remove all DC inputs from the product. 2. If you charge the product via a solar panel, check the open-circuit voltage (Voc) of the connected solar panel. The product allows a maximum DC input voltage of 28V. 3. Restart the product and keep it idle. Wait until the fault disappears.
Remove the load connected to the USB/DC 12V ports of the product. Wait until the fault disappears.

This Guide has been prepared in accordance with the EU Batteries Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. It is intended to clearly inform end users of their responsibilities regarding waste prevention, compliant disposal requirements, official recycling channels, safe handling procedures, and the potential risks associated with hazardous substances. Through this Guide, Jackery aims to fulfill its mandatory disclosure obligations under applicable regulations, promote battery recycling and resource recovery, and prevent environmental pollution and potential safety hazards. As part of our commitment to complying with Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries and waste batteries, we are committed to ensuring the safe handling and disposal of waste batteries. Choosing durable, repairable, and recyclable products can significantly reduce waste generation. Proper battery maintenance and care can also extend battery life and reduce the need for frequent replacement. When a battery approaches the end of its service life, proper disposal is essential. Batteries may contain hazardous substances that, if handled improperly, may harm the environment and pose risks to human health and safety.
The Role of End Users in Waste Prevention
End users can help extend battery service life and reduce waste generation at the source by choosing durable, repairable, and recyclable Jackery products and properly maintaining their batteries.
Purchase products according to actual needs

Select an energy storage product with an appropriate capacity based on your actual usage scenarios. Avoid unnecessary purchases or excessive stockpiling, which may result in batteries being left unused for extended periods and prematurely reaching the end of their service life.
Use Jackery energy storage devices properly

Follow the charging and discharging instructions provided in the product manual. Avoid overcharging, deep discharge, exposure to high temperatures or direct sunlight, and physical impact to help extend battery service life and reduce the generation of waste batteries.

If the device will not be used for an extended period, maintain the battery charge level between 20% and 60%. Store the device in a cool, dry environment and recharge it periodically to help slow battery degradation. Extending battery life and reducing the generation of waste batteries is one of the most important environmental responsibilities of every end user.
Separate Collection of Waste Batteries and Legal Obligations

Under applicable EU law, all Jackery waste lithium-ion batteries must be handled and disposed of in compliance with applicable requirements. End users are required to fulfill the following obligations:

You must dispose of waste batteries: 1. Separately from other waste streams, including mixed municipal waste; and 2. At designated separate collection points for waste batteries. Waste batteries must not be disposed of together with household waste or other mixed waste. They must be collected separately and taken to officially designated and compliant collection points.

At the end of their service life, batteries must only be returned through appropriate channels, including municipal recycling centers, authorized retailers, or official Jackery recycling channels. Do not disassemble, modify, or otherwise attempt to dispose of waste batteries yourself. Please cooperate with authorized recycling programs to ensure that waste batteries enter the appropriate recycling and recovery system.

Do not discard, landfill, or abandon waste batteries in open areas. Proper disposal helps reduce the risk of battery thermal runaway and prevents hazardous substances from contaminating soil and water. You can obtain information about the location of municipal collection centers from your local or municipal authorities. By recycling batteries, you help recover valuable materials and prevent environmental pollution.

Jackery's authorized dealers and offline retail stores within the European Union provide free recycling services for waste batteries and can accept waste batteries from Jackery energy storage products. Municipal recycling centers also provide ongoing collection services for waste batteries. Please note that, under applicable law, distributors are required to accept waste industrial batteries from end users free of charge and may not require end users to purchase, or have previously purchased, a new battery, regardless of the battery's chemistry, brand, or origin. Distributors must accept such batteries at their retail locations or in their immediate vicinity. These obligations also apply to distributors supplying batteries to end users through distance contracts. Such distributors must provide a sufficient number of collection points covering the territory of the relevant Member State, taking into account population size and density, the expected quantity of waste industrial batteries, and accessibility and proximity for end users.

Customers may use the recycling return service available through the Jackery official website and follow the instructions to safely package and ship used energy storage equipment for recycling. Jackery provides a recycling service that allows customers to return products that are used, no longer needed, or at the end of their service life for proper handling, recycling, or reuse. By ensuring that materials are handled responsibly, this service helps reduce environmental impact and prevent products from ultimately ending up in landfills. Jackery provides recycling services to all customers and verifies purchases of Jackery generators through authorized sales channels.

1. The recycling service is free of charge. The applicable shipping policy is as follows: 2. Returns during the warranty period: Jackery will cover the return shipping costs. 3. Returns of products outside the warranty period: The customer is responsible for the return shipping costs.

1. Safely place your device in a suitable shipping box and securely seal the package. 2. Clearly attach the return shipping label to the outside of the package. 3. Take the package to your nearest parcel drop-off location. 4. Cash on Delivery (COD) is not accepted.
Safety Instructions for Handling Used Batteries

Handling lithium-ion batteries involves a risk of fire. Please strictly follow the safety instructions below. Compliance with these safety instructions is important for protecting yourself and the environment. When handling waste batteries, particularly lithium-ion batteries, it is essential to understand the potential risks. Improper handling may result in overheating, fire, or other serious hazards.
Never crush, puncture, disassemble, or otherwise physically damage waste batteries. Damaged batteries may leak hazardous chemicals or catch fire.
Store batteries in an appropriate environment

Store batteries in a cool, dry, room-temperature, and well-ventilated area, away from high temperatures, water, and flammable or explosive materials to prevent short circuits and overheating. Do not expose batteries to excessive heat or water, as this may cause overheating or short circuits.

If handling a damaged or leaking battery, wear protective gloves and safety goggles and avoid direct contact with the electrolyte. If you notice any swelling, leakage, or unusual odor, exercise extreme caution when handling the battery and seek professional assistance.

If a battery shows signs of swelling, leakage, an unusual odor, or other abnormalities, immediately isolate it in a safe location and contact an official recycling channel. Do not attempt to handle or dispose of the battery yourself.
Emergency response in case of ﬁre
If a battery catches fire, use an appropriate fire extinguisher or sand to extinguish the fire. Do not use water to extinguish a lithium-ion battery fire, as this may worsen the situation.
Battery Contents and Environmental and Health Impacts

Jackery products are equipped with lithium-ion batteries, which may contain metals such as lithium, nickel, and cobalt, as well as organic electrolytes. Improper disposal may result in multiple risks.
If waste batteries are discarded improperly and electrolyte leaks, hazardous substances may enter soil and groundwater, causing soil and water contamination and damaging ecosystems and wildlife.

Battery electrolyte may be corrosive. Direct contact with skin or mucous membranes may cause irritation or chemical burns. Continued release of hazardous substances into the environment may also create long-term health risks.
Improper crushing, puncturing, or incineration of waste lithium-ion batteries may cause thermal runaway, fire, or other serious safety incidents, potentially resulting in burns and property damage.

The crossed-out wheeled bin symbol on a battery indicates that the battery must not be disposed of as unsorted household waste. At the end of its service life, the battery must be collected separately and handled through an appropriate recycling system. It must be taken to a designated municipal collection point or a dedicated collection system for recycling.

If Cd (cadmium) or Pb (lead) is indicated beneath the battery symbol, this means that the battery contains the corresponding heavy metal and must be subject to appropriate separate collection and recycling.
Battery model numbers, serial numbers, and production dates are used by recycling organiza- tions for sorting, inspection, grading, reuse, and material recovery.

All collected Jackery waste batteries are handled through qualified and compliant organizations in the European Union in accordance with applicable requirements. Unauthorized handling or disposal is prohibited. The subsequent processing of waste batteries may include the following three pathways:
Retired batteries are inspected and, where appropriate, repaired. Batteries that remain in good condition may be returned to service for further use.

Batteries whose capacity has degraded and which no longer meet the requirements for use in portable energy storage systems may, following appropriate assessment and screening, be used in lower-power energy storage applications.

Batteries that are no longer suitable for reuse are transferred to qualified and compliant recycling organizations in the European Union for the recovery of metal and other valuable materials, thereby supporting resource circularity. Individuals are prohibited from independently handling or disposing of waste lithium-ion batteries. All collected waste batteries are handled by qualified professional organizations in the European Union.
